title: Breaking a corruption totem heals the swamp around it – my AI-assisted action RPG made in Godot
author: DetectiveExisting803
selftext:
Hey! This is Proyecto Vil, a small action RPG I'm building in Godot 4 with a lot of AI help.



In this clip you clear the area around a corruption totem, break it, and the swamp heals around you: the purple rot turns back into grass. Each zone has totems like this, and breaking all of them opens the path to the boss.



How AI is involved:

\- Code: written together with Claude (I describe, test and fix)

\- Concept art: ChatGPT

\- 3D models: Meshy, rigged with Mixamo/Blender

\- Music and SFX: ElevenLabs



I'm not a professional dev, so I'd love honest feedback: does the "healing" moment read well? Is it satisfying, or does it need more impact?



I'm documenting the whole process in Spanish devlogs on YouTube if anyone's curious.

comments.author: dilberry
comments.body: Looks good - how did you refine the movement so well? It doesn't look like the Mixamo animations I've seen on there.

replies.author: DetectiveExisting803
replies.body:
Thanks! The base animations are actually Mixamo, but I don't play them raw. On top of them there's a procedural layer in Godot (a SkeletonModifier3D) that adjusts the bones every frame: feet are planted to match the real movement speed so they don't slide, the weapon stays locked in the hand, and the head turns toward enemies. Attacks also got longer swings and small reactions when you get hit.



I also record gameplay and have an AI review the footage to point out what looks off (sliding feet, stiff poses), then fix it with Claude. Lots of small iterations rather than one big trick.
